abstract.t: SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks) is a path-aware inter-domain network architecture in which an endpoint chooses the path of its packets. A service can publish SCION addresses next to its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in DNS Service Binding (SVCB) and HTTPS records. This document specifies how a Happy Eyeballs Version 3 client uses these addresses. SCION addresses form a third address family, so that the client connects over SCION where SCION works and over IP where it does not. Because one path can fail while others work, the client attempts a SCION address on up to three paths that differ from each other (two by default). It starts these attempts a short delay apart (50 milliseconds by default), each as a separate connection, and uses the first attempt that succeeds. This document is Experimental. It states what is to be measured to confirm or change these defaults.
